I fixed the bug: with smarty on, `![x\"x](x)` now renders `

`, the same as the unescaped version. The full suite still has 8 failures, but the same 8 fail on the code before my change. They're HTML-block tests in `test_html_blocks.py` and `test_md_in_html.py` and have nothing to do with escaping. **Cause.** A backslash escape like `\"` is held as a placeholder while the inline patterns run. `UnescapePostprocessor` (`markdown/postprocessors.py:125`) turns it back into the real character only *after* the document has been converted to HTML text. So when the placeholder sits inside an attribute such as `alt`, `title` or `href`, the `"` comes back raw and is never written as `"`. Smarty adds `"` and `'` to the characters a backslash can escape, which is why the issue only shows up with it. **Fix** (`markdown/inlinepatterns.py`). `Pattern.unescape()` already cleans up placeholders before values are stored as attributes; links, images, autolinks and automail links all go through it. It now also turns backslash-escape placeholders back into real characters, so the normal HTML output escapes them correctly. The placeholder pattern is a new `ESCAPE_PLACEHOLDER_RE` constant. Plain text is unchanged: `a\"b` still gives `

a"b

`, because the postprocessor still handles text. Side effects: - **Without smarty:** an escaped `\>` in alt text now comes out as `>` instead of a raw `>`. Both are valid HTML. - **Automail links:** an escape inside an address used to become a broken numeric entity (``); now the real character is kept. **Tests** - New `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` covers `\"` and `\'` in image alt text, `\"` in a link title, and `\"` in plain text. The alt and title `\"` tests fail without the fix and pass with it. - `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_images.py` gets one test for `\>` in alt text without smarty. **Test runs** - With `python -m unittest discover tests`: 977 tests, 8 failures, the same ones listed above. - With `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests`, collection stops with an error in `test_md_in_html.py`, both before and after my change. Skipping that file, the result is 4 failed and 675 passed. Nothing is committed.
